---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Self-Funded R&D Intensity
EXPRESSION: SUB(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at)), RANK(RATIO(sstk, at)))
HYPOTHESIS: Intangible investment carried on internal cash flow is credible innovation, whereas equity-funded intangible spending is contaminated by market-timed issuance; the spread between R&D intensity and equity-issuance intensity isolates the productive component and earns positive abnormal returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: R&D intensity alone is a known positive-return characteristic and share issuance alone is a known negative one, but the interaction matters because the same R&D dollar is priced very differently when it is bankrolled by new equity sold at a high valuation. Ranking both channels before differencing makes the two themes comparable in units and keeps the signal robust to scaling outliers. COALESCE treats non-reporting firms as zero R&D, which is the standard economic convention and preserves broad coverage.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Debt-Disciplined Innovation Funding
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(xrd, at)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(dltis, sstk), at)))
HYPOTHESIS: Among R&D-intensive firms, those tilting external funding toward debt rather than equity are monitored, cash-flow-confident innovators, while equity-tilted R&D funders are exploiting overvaluation; the product of R&D intensity and the debt-minus-equity funding mix identifies productive intangible financing.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Debt issuance requires servicing capacity and creditor scrutiny, so it is a costly signal when intangible assets provide little collateral, whereas equity issuance is cheapest precisely when the stock is rich. The multiplicative form makes the funding-mix tilt matter most where intangible investment is large, which is the exact conditioning the economic story requires.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Payout-Backed Knowledge Capital
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(prstkc, dvc), at), RATIO(TS_SUM(xrd, 5), at))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms that simultaneously return capital to shareholders and sustain a large stock of accumulated R&D are signaling that their intangible capital is internally financeable and undervalued; this joint configuration should outperform intangible-heavy firms that must absorb outside capital.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Negative net external financing (repurchases plus dividends) is a credible statement that management sees the shares as cheap, and it is most informative when the firm also owns a deep, hard-to-value knowledge stock that markets systematically underprice. Five-year cumulative R&D captures the intangible capital state rather than a single noisy annual flow, and SUMRANK combines the two themes with equal, outlier-resistant weight.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Externally Financed Goodwill Buildup
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(DELTA(gdwl, 1), at)), RANK(RATIO(ADD(dltis, sstk), at)))
HYPOTHESIS: Purchased intangibles (goodwill) created while the firm is simultaneously raising large amounts of debt and equity reflect overpayment for acquired intangible assets funded by cheap capital, and such firms subsequently underperform.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Goodwill is the accounting residual of acquisition prices, so its growth is a direct measure of how much the buyer paid above identifiable value; when that purchase is financed externally rather than from internal cash, agency and market-timing motives dominate and later write-downs follow. The multiplicative form is essential because organic goodwill-light growth or financing unaccompanied by acquisitions carries no such implication.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Issuance Against Fading Intangible Productivity
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(sstk, at)), RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(revt, intan), 5))))
HYPOTHESIS: Equity issuance is overvaluation-driven rather than investment-driven when the revenue productivity of the firm's existing intangible base is deteriorating; issuers with declining sales-per-intangible-dollar should earn the most negative subsequent returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: If intangible capital is still converting into revenue at an improving rate, new equity plausibly funds a positive-NPV innovation pipeline, but a multi-year decline in intangible productivity means the firm is capitalizing soft assets that no longer generate sales while tapping the market. The five-year TREND supplies the needed state-deterioration concept that a one-year change would measure too noisily, and the product form makes the productivity trend bite only where issuance is actually occurring.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Direction-Signed External Intangible Funding
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ADD(sstk, dltis), at)), SIGN(DELTA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: The same amount of external capital raised is good news when intangible investment intensity is rising (funds are being deployed into innovation) and bad news when intangible intensity is falling (funds are being raised opportunistically), so signing financing volume by the direction of R&D intensity separates productive from timed issuance.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This directly implements the economic story as a sign-switch rather than an additive blend: identical financing intensity maps to opposite predictions depending on whether the intangible investment program is expanding or contracting. Using SIGN of the change in R&D-to-sales avoids letting the magnitude of a volatile ratio dominate, while the ranked financing intensity supplies the economically meaningful scale of the interaction.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
